The smallest integer $ n > 1 $ such that $ n^{-1} \pmod{1050} $ exists is the smallest integer greater than 1 coprime to 1050. Since $ 1050 = 2 \times 3 \times 5^2 \times 7 $, $ n $ must not be divisible by 2, 3, 5, or 7. Checking sequentially: 2 (divisible by 2), 3 (divisible by 3), 4 (divisible by 2), 5 (divisible by 5), 6 (divisible by 2/3), 7 (divisible by 7), 8 (divisible by 2), 9 (divisible by 3), 10 (divisible by 2/5), and 11 is not divisible by any. Thus, the answer is $ \boxed{11} $.
